newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas says will exceed cost-cut target.
newsitem.headline: Qantas says will exceed cost-cut target.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd chief executive James Strong said on Sunday he expected the airline to exceed its cost-cut target for the year to June 30, 1997, last estimated by the company at $A430 million.
Aviation analysts expect Qantas to save about A$500 million in spending during the 1996/97 financial year.
Asked on Channel Nine's Business Sunday television programme whether Qantas would exceed $A500 million in cuts, Strong replied: "Well, we will exceed our target this year."

Qantas announced plans last week to invest A$560 million in upgrading its services, mainly on international flights, through new seating and interactive services such as video games, movies and possibly in-flight gambling.

Strong said the new investment plan did not affect the airline's cost-saving programme and the new spending initiative would be funded through cash flow and current debt facilities, with no new capital raising planned.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc.
